source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / Directorate General of Agriculture, "បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះសណ្តែកសៀង" [Soybean cultivation techniques], official extension manual, 2018
text:
Harvest section: most farmers rely on visible ripening signs rather than counting exact days, since seed size within a pod is not perfectly uniform, so growers are advised to watch for whole-plant color change (leaves and stems drying/yellowing) together with pod color change as the combined signal of maturity, rather than any single cue alone, and to harvest promptly once that point is reached since delayed harvest costs yield to shattering and pest damage.

Harvest is done either fully mechanized (combine harvester, photographed) or in mixed operations with hand-cutting followed by mechanical threshing. Post-harvest drying is done on tarpaulin/concrete drying floors, with the manual recommending drying to around 14–15% moisture before storage or sale, and noting an aluminium-sulphate-based storage treatment (10g per unit of stored produce, rate as printed) as one option for protecting stored seed from insect damage, applied per accepted safe-storage practice with attention to dosage.

National statistics close the manual: Cambodian average soybean yield is cited around 1.843 t/ha against a world average around 1.849 t/ha (essentially at parity), with total national soybean area cited around 43,000 ha (in the year referenced, 1996 per the source's own dating) rising toward roughly 22,71,000 ha equivalent figure as printed in a later year comparison (figures reproduced as printed; the manual's own year-labels for this comparison were not fully legible and should be treated as approximate). Two AVRDC-sourced varieties, DT84 and AGS73, are cited as giving average yields around 1,850 kg/ha under recommended practice.
